licence: Recreational Pilot Permit / Private Pilot Licence (Aeroplane)
subject: Navigation
learning_objective: Calculate the heading required to fly the reciprocal of an outbound track, given the outbound heading/track relationship.
question_text: If a heading of 250°M maintains your outbound track of 242°M, the required heading to maintain the reciprocal track back to your departure point would be
explanation: The outbound wind correction angle (WCA) is heading minus track: 250°M - 242°M = +8° (heading right of track). The reciprocal track is 242° + 180° = 062°M. For a reciprocal track, the same wind now has the opposite effect relative to the new track, so the WCA is subtracted rather than added: 062°M - 8° = 054°M.

incorrect_answer_explanations.A: 078°M applies the correction in the wrong direction and does not correspond to the correct reciprocal-track WCA logic.
incorrect_answer_explanations.B: 070°M does not correctly apply the 8° wind correction angle to the reciprocal track of 062°M.
incorrect_answer_explanations.C: 062°M is the reciprocal track itself, with no wind correction applied — it omits the necessary WCA adjustment.

regulation_reference: Standard dead-reckoning navigation theory as taught in Canadian PPL/RPP groundschool.
calculation_steps: Outbound WCA = heading - track = 250°M - 242°M = +8°. Reciprocal track = 242°M + 180° = 062°M. Reciprocal heading = reciprocal track - outbound WCA = 062°M - 8° = 054°M.
